# Critique — Pattern 9 (Recent Medical Activity)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Major Care Events (~10%), Routine Care Attendance (~10%), Diagnostic Testing & Immunizations (~20%), New Diagnoses, Transitions, & Insurance (~35%), and self-monitoring/lifecycle fillers (~25%). The time windows were handled consistently by defaulting to the "past 12 months" in the phrasing of every recent event question, preventing any ambiguity between "recent" and "lifetime" (which belong in condition-specific profiles). A few questions about ongoing care (e.g., awaiting scheduled surgeries or following up on abnormal results) came closest to boundaries, but were framed as current activities. Overlaps exist with almost all other patterns (such as mental health therapy, vaccinations, and imaging scans) because recent care contacts cross all physiological systems. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions where a "Yes" answer indicates proactive compliance with care guidelines (e.g., annual primary care visits, dental checks, up-to-date vaccinations) to maintain a polarity where `1` represents abnormality or lack of screening. We referenced HEDIS care quality measures for the routine check-up types, paraphrasing them neutrally. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your symptoms weekly...") as weekly logging is less standardized than formal diagnostic encounters.
